To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
experienced typists can learn to use a split keyboard as well as a flat keyboard in 2 h and that the split keyboard reduces wrist/hand pronatory posture.
the split keyboard design and wrist rest had no effect on performance, posture, or musculoskeletal pain.
the SA keyboard provided a more natural position for the hands and wrists, and the use of a split keyboard did not affect the performance of experienced typists.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the split, adjustable (split-A) keyboard and a wrist rest on experienced computer users′ performance, posture and musculoskeletal symptoms.
the effects of a split, adjustable computer keyboard and a wrist rest on performance, posture, comfort, and pain.
how to design computer input devices that are comfortable and efficient to use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a split keyboard design and wrist rest do not appear to provide significant performance advantages, and may even increase musculoskeletal discomfort.

the SA keyboard is a viable option for reducing wrist/hand pronations in computer work, and the use of a keyboard with an integrated wrist rest may reduce musculoskeletal discomfort in the wrists and hands, although it may not reduce discomfort in the upper back, shoulders, and neck.
there are no differences in performance, posture or pain between SA keyboard and a standard flat keyboard, and there are no differences between SA keyboard and SA keyboard with wrist rest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SA keyboard design is an acceptable alternative to the flat keyboard for experienced typists.

the split design of the SA keyboard provides a better fit with the natural anatomy of the hands and wrists and provides a more neutral posture for the hands, wrists, and forearms, and therefore is more comfortable than a flat keyboard.
the split keyboard design and a wrist rest can be used without a negative effect on the musculoskeletal system of experienced typists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the split, adjustable computer keyboard design provides advantages in reducing the wrist/hand pronated posture, but does not provide any advantages in reducing musculoskeletal pain.
a well-designed SA keyboard is a viable alternative to the flat keyboard for experienced typists.
the split keyboard can be used by experienced typists without a loss of performance, but it can provide advantages in reducing wrist/hand pronated posture.
